title: It's Not Too Late
author: Science of Reading Classroom
summary: A 10th grader reading at 35 wpm, 1st percentile skills improved through systematic instruction. Phonological awareness screening, explicit phonics, syllabication, accuracy-first work brought her to 100+ wpm, 96% accuracy in one year, jumping to 35th percentile comprehension. Breakthrough required trust and honoring her age while delivering foundational work. Adolescent struggling readers need evidence-based sequence with urgency, respect, and belief—not different processes. Systematic instruction transforms both reading and students' sense of what's possible.
points: Phonological awareness precedes decoding; older struggling readers have undiagnosed deficits.
Accuracy before speed; break guessing habits and ensure examination of every word part.
Relationship and trust enable vulnerability; students must feel safe.
Adolescent readers need evidence-based sequence honoring their age.
Intervention at 15 is not too late; it transforms possibility.
quotes: She had made it to 10th grade functionally illiterate.
We worked relentlessly to break the habit of guessing.
The day she broke 100, we both cried. It was proof.

Behind every older struggling reader is a student surviving without fundamental access.” “We change what they believe is possible for their lives.” Archived from Science of Reading Classroom on April 21, 2026 by Tim.
